title: European strategic autonomy and transatlantic dependence
discussion_signal: The post frames European autonomy as greater defense, industrial, and technological capacity within—not necessarily against—an alliance. It separates interoperability from asymmetric dependence and treats factories, supply chains, engineering, and production as strategic capability.
linked_research_question: How alliance commitment, domestic capacity, industrial dependence, and partner burden-sharing become distinct stages of strategic room and state consequence.
limits: Advocacy and analysis from a selected professional audience
No measured military readiness or alliance behavior
Policy recommendations are not observed implementation
